# sq-73 — Prefix cut contract: whole characters in every charset

Pin and document that ProfilePrefix (and Profile with MaxBytes) never cuts inside a character or a line terminator in any sniffed charset, and let a consumer recognise the first-record ceiling's refusal; requested for prism, which will switch to ProfilePrefix when it accepts non-UTF-8 input.

**Findings:**  · **Size:** M · **Tree:**

**2026-11-02** — [decision] Q4: expose the first-record refusal as an error-code property on SqualifyException (additive). Q5: do not report the prefix length in characters; document the cut contract only, no schema change. Decided by Jon R, 2026-11-02.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:** new charsets; changing where the cut falls for files that already cut correctly; a prefix length in characters (owner Q5); codes for other SqualifyException throw sites.

## Why

Owner (2026-11-02, from prism): a consumer cutting a text file to a byte budget must never split a character or a line terminator, whatever the encoding, so character and line counts stay right. prism (DangerDevices.Prism) reads only UTF-8 today and cuts its own 1 MiB prefix after the last LF, which is safe for UTF-8 because 0x0A never occurs inside a multi-byte sequence. prism decided (its D121) to switch to `Profiler.ProfilePrefix` when it first accepts a non-UTF-8 or CR-only format. `ProfilePrefix` already cuts in code units of the sniffed charset at LF, CR or CRLF; this slice makes that a pinned, documented contract a consumer can rely on, and makes the first-record ceiling's refusal something a consumer can tell apart from other failures.

## Failing tests

- `The_cut_never_splits_a_character`: for UTF-8 (2-, 3- and 4-byte sequences straddling MaxBytes), UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE (a surrogate pair and a CRLF straddling the limit), UTF-32LE/BE, with and without a BOM: the prefix decodes without replacement characters, ends at a terminator, and its line and character counts equal those of the same lines decoded from the whole file.
- `CR_only_and_mixed_terminators_cut_at_a_whole_line` (CR, LF, CRLF; a CR that ends the limit takes its LF).
- `A_first_record_over_the_ceiling_has_its_error_code`: for each charset above, `ProfilePrefix` with `MaxFirstRecordBytes` below the first record's length throws a `SqualifyException` whose `Code == SqualifyErrorCodes.FirstRecordTooLong`; another failure (for example a zero `MaxBytes`) has `Code == null`.
- `ProfilePrefix_and_Profile_agree` on the same files (descriptor equality), extended to the cases above.
